# Pilot amendment 4: retained timeout and fresh-session recovery

The local-target Codex trial reached the predeclared ten-minute cap after
committing the accepted greeting. A separately executed pinned checker passed
that exact source; no complete native readiness is inferred. Retain the timeout,
all usage, governance-only intermediate commit repair and unfinished native proof.

Before the next launch, declare a separate recovery run with a twenty-minute
cap, beginning at the prior claimed worktree/candidate and using the same stable
actor and natural objective: “Continue the in-progress fixture greeting update
and finish its required verification.” Do not provide a manual command sequence,
change native proof policy or silently extend the old run. The earlier host used
an ephemeral session, so this is repository-state recovery in a fresh session;
conversation resume and guaranteed provider cache state remain unobserved.

Keep the fixed independent greeting checker unchanged. Report the failed and
recovery runs together with additive observed wall/usage, and leave total cost
or human attention unknown when unavailable. A successful recovery cannot erase
the earlier failed trial. Warm repository/fresh-session punctuation work is a
different predeclared criterion, never pooled into the cold task denominator.
